subject: Route slice visualizer + ownership + exception playbook
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: jordan.lee@acmeapp.com; kira@obs-vendor.com
Date: Wed, 03 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Route slice visualizer + ownership + exception playbook

Team —

I want to start a short cross-functional ask to get a minimal, actionable "route slice visualizer" into the Console for Q2 cadence planning. The idea is a compact matrix view that lets product, SRE, and CS do three things without ad-hoc queries:

- Compare median/p95 latency and per-tenant cost for a list of routes (last 24h / 7d).
- Surface current owner and on-call for each route (owner metadata).
- Trigger an exception playbook when cost delta or latency regression exceeds thresholds.

Why now: a couple of customers (Acme) ran into sustained bursts last week; we lacked a fast UI to correlate route-level spikes to tenant vs model config changes. We ended up doing manual exports which took too long.

Ask: can infra/telemetry produce a minimal export and a small mock UI we can test with CS? Specifically:
1) Marcus — can you confirm whether we can include per-route token count, median/p95 latencies, model variant, and a tenant-aggregated cost column in the same export?
2) Karthik — I need guidance on how we attribute cost for routes that use shared batching (tenant attribution vs route-level amortization). Short note or pointer to existing docs is fine.
3) Grace — can you take point on owner naming on the UI and an initial canary roll plan for the team?

I've attached a mockup (route-matrix-mockup-v1.png) and a sample CSV export (example-export-tenant-costs.csv) with redacted tenant ids. If we can align on a minimal schema by EOD Monday, I can open a HubSpot ticket and a tiny UX spike (2w).

Thanks —
Olga
Olga Petrov
Product Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, jordan.lee@acmeapp.com
Date: Wed, 03 May 2028 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Route slice visualizer + ownership + exception playbook

Thanks, Olga — good call. Short answers:

- We can produce a nightly export (CSV/Parquet) with: route_id, route_name, tenant_id (nullable), model_variant, token_count, total_cost_usd, median_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, sample_rate, batch_size_distribution.
- Per-route cost will be approximate if batching is shared; we can include an amortized cost column and a confidence flag (high/medium/low).
- We can also include a small heuristic column for cache-hit-rate which might explain token cost deltas.

Caveats: the bundle size could be large if we include tenant-level rows for all tenants. For the UI we should surface aggregated route-level numbers with a top-ten tenants breakdown on demand.

I'll drop a link to a small extractor job I can run on demand and attach a sample export by EOD.

—Marcus
Principal Infra Engineer

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 May 2028 12:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Route slice visualizer + ownership + exception playbook

Olga — quick context on attribution:

- If routes share a GPU worker pool, token-to-cost mapping is noisy at micro-batch boundaries. The pragmatic approach is to use amortized cost per token (pool cost / total_tokens) and then multiply by route tokens. This is what Marcus called "amortized cost."
- For high-confidence billing (invoicing), we should avoid showing tenant-level invoice numbers in the UI; use estimates and a confidence badge.
- For the exception playbook: include a step to confirm (1) did batch sizes change?, (2) model variant changes, (3) any new tenant-level spikes (top 5 tenants). If confidence is low, route should not auto-escalate to infra on-call — instead open a P1 draft in PagerDuty with manual approval.

I'll write a short runbook stub and drop it in that Google Doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1yRouteVisualizer/preview (editable for the Observability PM group).

Karthik
Senior Systems PM

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 May 2028 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Route slice visualizer + ownership + exception playbook

Great — I can own the UI owner metadata and the canary rollout. Quick proposals:

- UI: Owner field should surface a primary owner (team@redwood) + on-call alias. Clicking the owner goes to a lightweight ownership card (name, pager, runbook link).
- Canary: start with internal-only flag (Console beta), then roll to 10% of customers (non-prod) for two weeks, then full rollout.
- Alerts: create two alert thresholds (cost delta > 50% vs 7d baseline; p95 latency > 2x baseline). For cost deltas, we should require the top-5 tenants breakdown to be visible before auto-creating a PagerDuty incident.

I'll coordinate with Growth CS for the 10% tenant cohort and can prepare the rollout doc by Friday.

Grace
Observability PM

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: jordan.lee@acmeapp.com, kira@obs-vendor.com
Date: Thu, 04 May 2028 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Route slice visualizer + ownership + exception playbook

Thanks all — summary and next steps: 

- Data: Marcus will run an extractor and share a sanitized CSV by EOD tomorrow. Schema agreed: route-level aggregates with optional per-tenant rows + amortized_cost_usd + confidence flag. (Marcus)
- Attribution/runbook: Karthik will draft a conservative exception runbook and add the confirmation gating steps. (Karthik)
- UX & Rollout: Grace will own owner metadata card and a beta-to-10%-to-full rollout plan; she will coordinate with CS for cohort selection. (Grace)
- External: Jordan, I appreciate the early heads-up — we'll use the beta to validate the matrices against your recent incident. Kira, if you can share any quick tips from your vendor console on top-tenant visibility, that will help.

I've filed HS-8742 and added the mockup/CSV to the doc. Link: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1yRouteVisualizer/preview. I'll convert the extractor into a recurring job after the beta if the data shape looks stable.

If there are no objections, I'll create the Console ticket and assign owners today.

—Olga
Product Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference
